Figure 18:Semantic Structure of the SWE Task Corpus.Each point represents a task, positioned by a t-SNE projection of embeddings of behavioral summaries and colored by programming language.
Labels describe communities identified in the original embedding space.
The figure shows 12K mined tasks and 1.5K synthesized feature tasks sampled from the full pool.

Figure 25:Predictable RL Evolution.Left: Predicted reward gains from the SFT checkpoint, compared to realized gains through RL, across components targeting different principles.
Predictions are made using a replicator equation with a learning constant fit to a single run.
Scatter shows distribution across 318 post-training runs, large symbols represent the final alignment teacher.
Right: Same equation applied to forecasting grader-detected misbehaviors, shaded band = forecast±\pmSE, dots = observed.
Changes in reward function (green circles) accurately predict squashing of misbehavior.

Figure 37:Memory allocation per B300 GPU (268.6 GiB) after model load.
Each configuration reserves 90% of HBM; KV cache uses the space remaining after weights and other allocations.
Labels inside bars show GiB; right-hand labels show replica-wide KV capacity in full-attention tokens.
Rows are sorted by KV capacity.

Figure 38:8k/1k scenario: Output throughput per GPU versus interactivity on NVIDIA B300 GPUs.
Each point represents a concurrency level, labeled c8–c256 by the number of concurrent requests.
Panel (a) uses each checkpoint’s smallest deployment: four GPUs for FP8 and NVFP4, and eight for BF16.
Panel (b) uses eight GPUs for all checkpoints.
Dotted lines mark 50 and 100 tok/s/user.
Points higher and farther right indicate better performance.

Figure 39:AgentX replay: output throughput per GPU versus interactivity on NVIDIA B300 GPUs.
Points are labeled by the number of concurrent sessions.
Panel (a) uses four GPUs for FP8 and NVFP4, and eight for BF16; panel (b) uses eight GPUs for all checkpoints.
The dotted line marks 50 tok/s/user.
Points higher and farther right indicate better performance.
